To

All Zonal Offices.

Sub:- Review of 7-A Inquiries pending for more than 3 years-
Regarding.

Sir/Madam,

Please refer to the email dated 03.02.2021 followed by Head Office letter
no. even dated 23.06.2021 and subsequent e-mail/reminders dated
25.06.2021, 15.07.2021 and 27.07.2021 on above noted subject and also
the previous instructions issued on 03.01.2019 on pending 7A cases. Time
and again higher authorities have expressed serious concern about long
pendency of 7A cases specially for over 5 years.

2. It is deeply regretted that in spite of so many letters and
reminders and introduction of the virtual hearing mode for quasi judicial
inquiries from October, 2020, no significant steps or major actions have
been taken by the Zonal Offices to review and bring down the pendency
of 7A/14B cases pending beyond three years and five years.

3. That several cases are pending in r/o non-functional / closed
establishments in which the whereabouts of employers is not known due
to which the summons / notices are not served and no report regarding
the amount due from establishment is available on record to conclude the
proceedings. Thus basic legal requirements for initiation of cases are not
fulfilled but cases are going on for years. In the various review meetings,
it was informed by few Regional Offices that they have resorted to issue
of public notice in such cases to invite information from the employers /
ex-employees and general public regarding the disbursement of wages
and employment of persons during the period of inquiry and final decision
has been taken according to the response to the public notice. It appears
that all Zonal / Regional Offices have not taken such action resulting in
huge pendency of cases.

4 . In view of the above it is directed that all ACCs-in-charge of ZO shall:

6.

a. review all 7A cases pending for over 5 years on fortnightly basis
and furnish the details of such cases to Head Office along with
name of assessing officers, the reasons of pendency and the actions
taken by the Adjudicating Officer to dispose them within the time
period stipulated by the Head Office guidelines issued from time to
time, the specific remarks of their respective supervisory officers
regarding the efforts made by them to ensure compliance with the
HO guidelines.

b. time bound disposal of all cases pending for more than 5 years by

30.09.2021 and all cases pending for more than 3 years by
31.12.2021; and

c. advise all Adjudicating Officers within their jurisdiction to complete

the 7A inquiries in a time-bound manner considering the provisions
of section 125 of the Code on Social Security, 2020.

d.In case it is required the officers not clearing pending cases as per

targets their continuity in compliance function be reviewed.

A comprehensive report in this regard along with specific

recommendations of ACC-in-charge of the ZO and _ actions
taken/contemplated against erring officers may also be furnished to this
office by 31.08.2021.

Yours faithfully,

2
Jag Mohan)
